newsitem.title: UK: Euro veg oils close mostly higher in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Euro veg oils close mostly higher in quiet trade.

text.p: Closing European vegetable oil prices were mostly higher on Tuesday in quiet trading.
News that Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto has been sacked produced little reaction among traders.
"Reaction has been much the same here as in Malaysia, no one is talking about it," said a trader.
Traders said the state-run Ghee Corp of Pakistan (GCP) has not been active recently, but if private buyers want palm oil they would buy regardless of who was in power.

"There may be one or two problems over payment, which always seems to happen whenever there is any political unrest in Pakistan, but they have not been very active lately so people are not concerned," said another trader.
Crude palm oil cif Europe closed $2.50 to $7.50 up with buyers showing a little more interest during the afternoon.
Nov crude palm oil traded at $542.50 and $545 with a switch between Nov and Dec reported earlier in the day when $537.50 was paid for Nov and $527.50 for Dec.
Refined palm oil was mixed with RBD oil $2.50 down and olein $2.50 up.
Slow shipments from origin supported coconut oil prices with closing sellers $15 higher after afloat fetched $780 to $790, Oct/Nov $760, Nov/Dec 735 and Dec/Jan $735 a tonne cif.
Palmkernel oil was $12.50 higher in a tradeless market.
Dutch soy oil and rape oil closed 0.50 guilders up after Dec rape oil traded at 91 guilders a 100 kg fob ex-mill.
Based on sellers prices rape oil is at a premium of 3.50 to four guilders over soy oil against 3.5 to 4.5 guilders at Monday's close.
